sw-1.1.summary: Phase 1 (The page without Kiro Crew). One command dispatch for both servers. See SW5.1, SW5.2, SW10.2, SW10.3; §D4, §D9.
acceptance: The app backend's existing tests pass unchanged; a new test runs one write and one observe operation through the app backend and straight through `dispatchCommand` with an `owner-session` claim and gets the same results; an unoffered operation gets the same 403 message from both; each reader-using operation, run with its reader absent, returns a "Needs Kiro Crew" result and throws nothing; `instance.view` returns `host: "kirocrew"` from the app backend.

sw-1.2.summary: Phase 1 (The page without Kiro Crew). The SDK stand-in, the second bundle and Avoozl's themes. See SW1, SW2, SW6; §D2, §D3, §D6.
acceptance: The type test fails on a changed stand-in signature and passes as built; the source test fails on a view importing `@kirocrew/app-sdk` or the stand-in directly; the import-specifier fixture for `dist/index.mjs` and `dist/panel.mjs` matches; `host-classes.test.mjs` runs against `dist/standalone/app.css` with no skip and passes; the variable test finds every `var(--…)` name in both themes; the contrast test passes in both; the path scan finds no home folder or worktree path in `dist/standalone/`; screenshots of Home, Plans and Settings at 390 and 1280 px, light and dark, go to the owner.

sw-1.3.summary: Phase 1 (The page without Kiro Crew). `avoozl serve` on loopback with the owner link. See SW3, SW4, SW5.3, SW5.4, SW5.5; §D5, §D10.
acceptance: Tests on Linux, macOS and Windows: the listener's address is `127.0.0.1`; `--host`, `--bind` and `AVOOZL_HOST` each refuse to start; a taken `--port` exits with "port N is in use"; a link works once, fails after use and after 10 minutes with the same 403; the cookie has `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, no `Domain`, and a port in its name; a POST with the cookie and no CSRF header, a wrong `Origin`, a missing `Origin`, `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`, `text/plain`, and a `Host: evil.example:<port>` request are each refused with 403; `OPTIONS` gets 403; no response has an `Access-Control-Allow-*` header and every one has the SW4.8 headers; each app backend principal header and a bearer header with no cookie gets 401; `demo.status` works; a search of the log, `serve.json` and the database after the run finds no token, cookie or CSRF value; `avoozl serve` and `serve link` with `AVOOZL_CHILD=1` are refused; the sandbox test shows the state folder outside a child's read and write roots.

sw-1.4.summary: Phase 1 (The page without Kiro Crew). Open chat as a process session, Kiro Crew-only states and browser notices. See SW7, SW8, SW10.1, SW10.4; §D7, §D9.
acceptance: UI tests on the standalone page: Ask for help in Settings › Content rules opens the dialog with the message and the `assist` role, and Start, with a fake `process` executor, records one read-only session request in the workspace root and shows its process view; `openChat` with `autoSend: true` starts nothing until Start; with no approved harness the dialog offers Copy and starts nothing; `session.open` from MCP and from an `agent-tool` principal is refused; every SW10.1 feature shows "Needs Kiro Crew" and no error; a pinned `kirocrew` task opens one Needs you item across three ticks; with notices on and a fake `Notification`, two new Needs you items give two notices and a reload gives none; screenshots go to the owner.

sw-1.5.summary: Phase 1 (The page without Kiro Crew). The supervisor hosts the page. See SW9; §D8.
acceptance: Tests: with `serve.enabled` the supervisor starts the server child and records its pid and port; a killed child is restarted on the same fixed port; the child prints no link; `avoozl status` shows the origin; `serve.*` in `.avoozl.json` is refused naming the key; the supervisor process itself has no listening socket.

sw-p1.summary: Phase 1 (The page without Kiro Crew). Proof: Avoozl runs a task end to end with no Kiro Crew, from its own page. See SW1 to SW10; §D1, §D5, §D7.
acceptance: Expected: (1) the page loads with no console error and no CSP report, in light and dark; (2) the task lands and the message reaches the child; (3) a read-only `assist` session starts and its view shows its log; (4) every attempt is refused and changes nothing; (5) the server comes back on the same port, the old session is gone and a new link signs in; `lsof` or `ss` shows only `127.0.0.1:<port>` listening for the server.
